name: Garden State Eats: Restaurants
subtitle: NJ Diners, Pizza & Pork Roll
description:
New Jersey's restaurants, from a dining car on Route 46 to a clam bar down the Shore.

Garden State Eats is a free guide to eating in New Jersey: 13 diners, 5 places for pork roll, egg and cheese, 7 for tomato pie, 10 hot dog stands, 8 delis for subs and sloppy joes, 7 BYOB restaurants and 9 Shore clam bars and seafood shacks, each checked by hand. Behind them, 21,754 restaurants, cafés, bars and bakeries in 549 towns, each filed under its own municipality and the local health department that inspects it. No account, no ads.

JERSEY GUIDES
• Diners: vintage dining cars and the big highway diners.
• Pork Roll, Egg & Cheese: Taylor ham up north, pork roll down south.
• Tomato Pie: Trenton's, cheese first and tomatoes on top.
• Hot Dogs: rippers, Italian hot dogs and roadside stands.
• Subs & Sloppy Joes, BYOB, Boardwalk Classics and Shore Seafood.
• Award winners: 8 James Beard semifinalists, finalists and America's Classics.

HEALTH INSPECTIONS
Every New Jersey restaurant inspection ends in an official placard: Satisfactory, Conditionally Satisfactory or Unsatisfactory. The Monmouth County Office of Public Health and the Camden County Department of Health post theirs online, and the app shows the latest one for 1,484 places, word for word, with its date. Everywhere else it names the health department that inspects the town. The app computes no grades.

FIND IT FAST
• Sort by distance, or browse the map by guide.
• Search by name, town (Iselin finds Woodbridge's Oak Tree Road), street or dish: "pork roll red bank", "route 9 diner".
• Filter by town or cuisine, or hide chains.
• Save places, and find hand-checked places from iPhone search (Spotlight).

LIVE DETAILS FROM APPLE MAPS
Tap "Ratings, hours & photos" on any place to open Apple Maps' own place card, with current hours, photos, ratings and directions.

HOW THE LISTS ARE BUILT
Every guide place was checked by hand in October 2026: a dated 2025 or 2026 source names it (local news, a food site or the place's own site), or an older one does and its county health department inspected it in 2025 or 2026. The rest come from Overture Maps open data, keeping the kinds of listing that held up best when checked. Website links are checked too. Nothing is ranked by star ratings.

PRIVATE BY DESIGN
No account, no tracking, no ads. Your location, if you share it, only sorts lists on your device. Saved places stay on your device.

Places open and close, and Shore places keep summer hours, so check before you go. Spot a mistake? Email nick@eatsranked.com.

An independent app, not affiliated with any restaurant, chain or government agency (including the State of New Jersey, the NJ Department of Health, the Division of Alcoholic Beverage Control, Monmouth County, Camden County and any local health department), or with the James Beard Foundation. James Beard Foundation and James Beard Award are trademarks of the James Beard Foundation. Place data from Overture Maps Foundation (CDLA Permissive 2.0) and others; sources and licenses are on the About tab.

reviewNotes:
1. Purpose and audience: Garden State Eats is a free guide to restaurants in New Jersey. Its focus is the state's own food: 13 diners, 5 places for pork roll, egg and cheese, 10 hot dog stands, delis, BYOB restaurants and Shore seafood, each checked by hand in October 2026 against a public source. It also lists 21,754 restaurants, cafés and bars statewide, each with the local health department that inspects it, and the official inspection placard for 1,484 places whose county posts ratings online. It is for New Jersey residents and visitors deciding where to eat, with no ads, account or tracking.

2. How to use it (no login, no setup, no sample files needed):
- Home → Diners (or Pork Roll, Egg & Cheese, Hot Dogs, Shore Seafood, Health Inspections, James Beard Honors, Near Me) → tap any place.
- On a place, tap "Ratings, hours & photos" to open Apple Maps' own place card through MapKit. Directions, Call and Website are below it, then the place's health inspection section.
- Search from the Home search box by name, town, street or dish ("pork roll red bank", "route 9 diner").
- The Map tab shows each guide as pins. "My location" and the Nearest sort use location only if allowed, on the device.
- The heart saves a place on the device, under the Saved tab. The About tab lists the data sources, licenses and the independence statement.
- On iPad, a sidebar replaces the tabs.
- Location: if you're outside New Jersey (as App Review usually is), the map says so and stays on New Jersey, and distance sorting still works from where you are.
- "Garden State" is the short Home Screen name of "Garden State Eats: Restaurants".

3. External services and data:
- Apple MapKit: maps, local search to find a place's Apple Maps listing, and Apple's place card for live hours, photos and ratings.
- Core Location: optional, on-device only, for distance sorting.
- Core Spotlight: on-device indexing so places appear in iPhone search.
- Data updates: once a day at most, the app checks the website below for newer restaurant data and downloads it. Requests carry no location or identifiers.
- No backend, accounts, analytics, advertising, payments or AI services.
- Data sources: Overture Maps Foundation open place data (CDLA Permissive 2.0, with Foursquare-sourced records under Apache 2.0 and AllThePlaces under CC0; license texts are in the app); the New Jersey Department of Health's directory of local health departments; the Monmouth County Office of Public Health's and Camden County Department of Health's public inspection search pages (each place's latest rating and date only); U.S. Census Bureau municipal boundaries; James Beard Foundation award records (facts only); and our own research of public websites and local news.
- The website with the privacy policy and support page is static and hosted on GitHub Pages: https://nickstrom5.github.io/new-jersey-eats/

4. Regional differences: none. The content covers New Jersey; the app is offered in the United States and works the same everywhere.

5. Regulated or protected material: the app is not in a regulated industry and includes no protected third-party material. The data is open-licensed or public record, with attribution and licenses on the About tab. Ratings, hours and photos are shown only inside Apple's own place card through MapKit; the app stores no ratings or reviews. Inspection placards are shown exactly as the county health departments published them, with their dates, and the app never computes grades. Every website link was checked before release, and adult venues and gaming parlors are excluded. The app is independent and not affiliated with any restaurant, agency or the James Beard Foundation.
